body.en: A single integral accumulates over an interval; a double integral accumulates a function over a two-dimensional region — most concretely, the volume trapped under a surface \( z=f(x,y) \).

Partition a region \( R \) into small cells of area \( \Delta A \), sample \( f \) in each, and sum. The double integral is the limit as the cells shrink:

\[ \iint_{R} f\,dA=\lim_{\Delta A\to 0}\sum_{i,j} f(x_i,y_j)\,\Delta A. \]

Over a rectangle \( R=[a,b]\times[c,d] \), a double integral equals an iterated integral, and the order may be swapped:

\[ \iint_{R} f\,dA=\int_a^b\!\!\int_c^d f(x,y)\,dy\,dx=\int_c^d\!\!\int_a^b f(x,y)\,dx\,dy. \]

body.en:
For circular regions, polar coordinates simplify everything — but the area element gains a factor of \( r \):

\[ \iint_{R} f\,dA=\iint f(r\cos\theta,\,r\sin\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta. \]

That extra \( r \) is the Jacobian of the polar change of variables, and forgetting it is the most common error in the topic.

Evaluate \( \displaystyle\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^2 (x+2y)\,dx\,dy \).

Integrate in \( x \) first, treating \( y \) as constant:

\[ \int_0^1\Big[\tfrac{x^{2}}{2}+2xy\Big]_0^2 dy=\int_0^1(2+4y)\,dy=\big[2y+2y^{2}\big]_0^1=4. \]

label.en: Worked example 14.B — Area of a disk in polar

body.en:
Confirm the area of the unit disk \( x^{2}+y^{2}\le 1 \) using a polar double integral.

\[ \iint_{R} dA=\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\int_0^1 r\,dr\,d\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}\tfrac12\,d\theta=\pi. \]

caption.en: Rectangular region of integration \(R = [0, 2] \times [0, 1]\) in the \(xy\)-plane for double integral evaluation.

body.en:
Polar Area Element (Jacobian r): In polar coordinates, \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\). Omitting the extra factor of \(r\) is the single most common error in multivariable calculus!

Reversing Order of Integration: You CANNOT merely swap the integral signs and limits when the region is non-rectangular: \(\int_0^1 \int_x^1 f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \ne \int_x^1 \int_0^1 f(x,y)\,dx\,dy\). You MUST sketch the 2D domain and reconstruct the bounding functions from horizontal vs vertical slices.

Coordinate Transformations Jacobian: When substituting \(x = g(u, v)\), \(y = h(u, v)\), always multiply the integrand by the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant \(|J(u, v)| = |x_u y_v - x_v y_u|\).

question.en: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\iint_R (2x + y)\,dA\) where \(R\) is the rectangular region \([0, 3] \times [1, 2]\).

solution.en:
Set up iterated integral:
\[ \int_1^2 \int_0^3 (2x + y)\,dx\,dy = \int_1^2 \left[ x^2 + xy \right]_0^3 dy = \int_1^2 (9 + 3y)\,dy \]
Integrate with respect to \(y\):
\[ \left[ 9y + \frac{3y^2}{2} \right]_1^2 = \left(18 + \frac{12}{2}\right) - \left(9 + \frac{3}{2}\right) = 24 - 10.5 = 13.5 = \frac{27}{2}. \]
